maya: quick sync — onboarding mistral-v2 (quantized q4_0). weights staged at s3://redwood-models/mistral/v2/q4_0/ — @jg can you confirm checksum and that the shard layout matches our split policy?

jg: checked the bucket, files present. sha256: 3f7a9c2b... matches manifest. shard pattern is model-0000..model-0007 (8 shards). one note: metadata.json missing `max_sequence` field, adding a quick PR to the training artifact repo.

maya: thanks. also opening a PR for the serving config now (#4321) — pinging reviewers. main things to validate: continuous batching knobs, cache policy (prefix vs full-kv), scheduler slo tokens, and max_tokens cap.

arjun: FYI I hit a tokenizer quirk when running local tokenization vs model wrapper: eos is encoded as two bytes in our tokenizer build, which makes our token count off by 1 in some edge cases. reproduction:
```
# reproducer snippet
text = "Hello"
toks = tokenizer.encode(text + "\n")
print(len(toks))  # 6 locally, model-side runtime expects 5
```
This causes KV cache indexing to be misaligned and continuous-batching to accidentally reuse prefixes incorrectly. Proposed fix: normalize_eos in tokenizer wrapper to single-token sequence or strip trailing newline before encode.

sasha: that explains a few flaky smoke failures. for config tuning i suggest:
```
continuous_batching: { min_batch: 3, max_batch_wait_ms: 25, max_concurrent_batches: 4 }
cache: { policy: "prefix_kv", ttl_seconds: 300, max_entries_per_model: 20000 }
scheduler: { slo_token_ms: 11, burst_capacity: 2 }
max_tokens: 1536  # start conservative for canary
```
Reasoning: keep latency tight (<30ms tail), min_batch=3 to avoid tiny micro-batches on low qps, ttl 300s for prefix hits.

maya: +1 on being conservative for canary. @arjun can you push the tokenizer normalization as a small patch to the model-adapter lib? we'll run smoke locally then canary.

arjun: will do. patch will: 1) add normalize_eos flag default true, 2) add unit test for edge-case sequences. also adding one-off migration for existing cached entries (invalidate prefix caches for mistral-v2).

lin: canary plan: route 2% traffic to mistral-v2 for 30 minutes -> check latency, token cost, and model quality on the gold prompts set. smoke tests to run before canary:
- ./tools/smoke_onboard.sh --model mistral-v2 --batch 4
- run tok-checker (new arg `--normalize-eos`)
- run perf sampler (1000 requests) to collect p95/p99
I'll also set a rollback window and auto-fail if p99 latency > 2x baseline or token error rate > 0.5%.

maya: perfect. i'll assign reviewers on #4321: @jg and @sasha. can you both take a look today? :)

jg: on it, will review the weight manifest change + serving config.

sasha: review in a bit. quick Q — do we want to bump max_tokens to 2048 for internal customers? that ups memory pressure and changes kernel selection heuristics. prefer 1536 for the public canary.

maya: agree. 1536 for canary, revisit after metrics.

deploy-bot: canary scheduled: mistral-v2 -> traffic 2% starting 1859129400 UTC. automated smoke run queued.

lin: leaving a note in the runbook: invalidate prefix cache after tokenizer patch, rehydrate after successful canary.

maya: cool — thanks team. small checklist for follow-ups: 
- arjun: tokenizer PR + cache invalidation patch
- jg: manifest update commit + checksum confirmation (done)
- sasha: config review + perf tuning notes
- lin: smoke + canary orchestration
I'll post a final sign-off here after the smoke passes. :thumbsup:
